hints: Notice the X to Y leg gives both distance $3.0\text{ m}$ and work $150\text{ J}$, so you can find the constant frictional force.
Use $W = Fd$ with constant $F$ to find $F$ from X to Y, then use the $200\text{ J}$ work to find the Y to Z distance.
Use the right angle at Y and the two side lengths to find the straight distance XZ, then compare $W_P$ with $W_Q = F \times XZ$.
walkthrough: Find the constant frictional force from X to Y using $W = Fd$. $F = W_{XY}/d_{XY} = 150/3.0 = 50\text{ N}$.
Find the distance Y to Z from its work. $d_{YZ} = W_{YZ}/F = 200/50 = 4.0\text{ m}$.
Find the direct distance XZ. The diagram is right-angled at Y with sides $3.0\text{ m}$ and $4.0\text{ m}$, so $XZ = \sqrt{3.0^2+4.0^2} = 5.0\text{ m}$.
Calculate work for each route. For P via Y: $W_P = 150+200 = 350\text{ J}$. For Q direct: $W_Q = F \times XZ = 50 \times 5.0 = 250\text{ J}$.
Extra work for P is $W_P - W_Q = 350-250 = 100\text{ J}$. This is option A.

options.A: Work for P is $150+200=350\text{ J}$ and work for Q is $50 \times 5.0=250\text{ J}$, so extra is $100\text{ J}$.
options.B: This is the work for Q alone, $F \times XZ = 250\text{ J}$, not the difference between P and Q.
options.C: This is the total work for P, $150+200=350\text{ J}$, not the extra work compared with Q.
options.D: This adds P and Q incorrectly as $350+250=600\text{ J}$ instead of subtracting to find the extra work.
